mainTopic: When can entering a house with a מת bring two liabilities at once, and from which פסוק do we learn that טומאת מת begins only at death (including the question of a גוסס)?
overview: The גמרא first asks how someone entering a house with a מת can be liable twice: once for becoming טמא and once for entering. The problem is timing. Some part of the body always goes in first and makes him טמא, so the full entry comes too late. רבי אלעזר and then רבא suggest ways of entering all at once, but each is knocked down: the nose or the toes always lead. רב פפא answers with a person carried in inside a closed container whose cover is then opened. מר בר רב אשי answers with someone who dies while the visitor is already sitting inside. Then a ברייתא teaches from two פסוקים, להחלו and במותם, that טומאת מת begins only at death. רבי יוחנן says the two sources differ only in which פסוק is used. ריש לקיש says they differ about a גוסס. The גמרא shows that each side has a use for both words, and it ends by answering a משנה: a גוסס does not make others טמא, but on the להחלו view a כהן is already profaned by him.

steps.title: Entering a house: the person is impure before he is fully inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges double liability for entering a house: once the hand enters, the person is already טמא, so the full entry adds nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a house too: as soon as he puts his hand in, he becomes impure. So when the rest of him comes in, he is already impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the idea that someone entering a house with a מת gets two punishments. His hand goes in first and makes him טמא before the rest of him enters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate violations need two separate moments that count: becoming טמא, and entering while טמא. If the hand already made him טמא, then when his body enters he is just a טמא person walking in. The challenge is that the two events never line up.

keyTerms.meaning: he became impure (טמא)
enters
ritually impure
since / as soon as

phrases.english: In a house too,
phrases.notes: He means a house with a dead body inside, where we want to say he gets two punishments.

phrases.english: once he puts in his hand, he becomes impure,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי עָיֵיל כּוּלֵּי, הַאי טָמֵא הוּא!
phrases.english: so when all of him enters, this one is already impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the timing problem about double liability in a house.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that entering a house with a מת brings two liabilities (טומאה and ביאה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hand enters first and makes him טמא, so by the time he fully enters he is already impure and the two events are not simultaneous.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: hand alone versus whole body at once
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that if only the hand went in, there is liability for טומאה only. If the whole body went in together, טומאה and ביאה come at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: if he put in his hand, he is liable for impurity but not for entering. If he joined his body together and went in all at once, impurity and entering come together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that the double liability applies only when the person goes in with his whole body at once, not hand first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hand alone can make you טמא, but a hand alone is not 'entering.' So רבי אלעזר pictures someone moving his whole body in together, so that becoming טמא and entering happen at one instant.

keyTerms.meaning: joined together / brought in together
impurity, here meaning liability for becoming טמא
entering, here meaning liability for entering
there is / there is not
together with each other, at the same time

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
If he put in his hand,
there is liability because of impurity,
but there is none because of entering.
But if he brought his whole body in together,
impurity and entering come at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the timing problem from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the double liability to a specific way of entering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any entry into a house gives two liabilities, even though the hand goes in first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a whole-body entry, done all at once, makes טומאה and ביאה simultaneous.

steps.title: The nose always goes in first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי אלעזר: the nose always enters before the rest of the body, so impurity still comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is impossible that his nose would not go in first, and then impurity would come down on him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's answer. Even when you walk in 'all at once,' your nose sticks out ahead and goes in first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same problem from step 1 comes back in a smaller form. A tiny part of the body, the nose, still enters first and makes him טמא. So the full entry still comes too late to be a second violation.

keyTerms.meaning: it is impossible
his nose
first
comes down / takes hold

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא עָיֵיל חוֹטְמוֹ בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: But it is impossible that his nose would not enter first,
and impurity would come down on him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא עָיֵיל חוֹטְמוֹ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nose sticks out and enters first, so impurity still comes before full entry.

steps.title: רבא: entering with the body standing upright
steps.stepSummary: רבא repeats the hand/body distinction, picturing the person entering his body upright so the head does not lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: if he put in his hand, he is liable for impurity but not for entering. If he brought in his body, impurity and entering come together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries a new version of the answer. He pictures the body going in standing straight, so the nose does not poke in first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the same rule as רבי אלעזר: a hand gives only טומאה, while a body entry gives both. The change is in how the body enters, upright and not leaning forward, to get around the nose problem.

keyTerms.meaning: brought in / put in
his body

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
If he put in his hand,
there is liability because of impurity,
but there is none because of entering.
If he brought in his body,

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְאָה וּבִיאָה בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָא אָתְיָין.
phrases.english: impurity and entering come at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer after רבי אלעזר's was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the body entry to avoid the nose leading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A whole-body entry always lets the nose go first.
steps.terutzMaskana: An upright body entry lets טומאה and ביאה happen together.

steps.title: The toes always go in first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא: even standing upright, the toes enter first and make him טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is impossible that his toes would not go in first, and then impurity would come down on them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. When you step into a house, your toes cross in before the rest of you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of attack as step 3. Whatever way a person walks in, some body part leads, so a natural entry can never make טומאה and ביאה exactly simultaneous.

keyTerms.meaning: fingers / toes
his foot / leg

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is being picky for no reason. The whole question is whether the two events happen at the very same instant, so any body part that goes in first ruins the case.

phrases.english: But it is impossible that there would not enter
the toes of his foot first,
and impurity would come down on them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא עָיֵיל אֶצְבְּעָתָא דְכַרְעֵיהּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down רבא's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The toes cross in first, so impurity still comes before full entry.

steps.title: רב פפא: carried in inside a closed container that is then opened
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the case is someone carried into the house inside a closed chest, box or cabinet, and a friend opens the cover over him. At that moment he becomes טמא and counts as entering together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: for example, he entered inside a chest, a box or a cabinet, and his friend came and opened the cover over him. Then impurity and entering come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a case where the two events really do happen together. The person is already inside the house, but sealed in a protective container, and the cover is opened all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he is sealed in the container, the impurity cannot reach him, and he does not count as being in the tent with the מת. When the cover is opened, his whole body is exposed at one instant. So he becomes טמא and counts as 'entering' at exactly the same moment, and the leading-body-part problem disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: a chest, a box and a cabinet (large containers that can block impurity)
opened / uncovered
the cover or roof of the container
for example / such as the case where

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
For example, where he entered in a chest, a box or a cabinet,
phrases.notes: These are big closed containers that keep the impurity from reaching the person inside.

phrases.english: and his friend came
and opened the cover above him,
so that impurity and entering come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּכְנַס בְּשִׁידָּה תֵּיבָה וּמִגְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both body-entry answers fail, it gives a case with no leading body part.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an unusual case where exposure happens to the whole body at once.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every entry into a house has some body part going in first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being uncovered inside a protective container makes טומאה and ביאה happen together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that double liability does exist in a house, but only in unusual cases where the timing truly lines up.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: someone dies while he is already inside
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the case is someone who entered while a person inside was dying. When that person died, the visitor became טמא and counted as being in a tent with a מת at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: for example, he entered while someone was dying, and that person's soul left while he was sitting there. Then impurity and entering come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי offers a second way the two events can happen together. The house has no מת when he walks in, and the death happens while he is sitting there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dying person (גוסס) is still alive, so the house is not yet a tent with a מת. The moment the person dies, the visitor is fully inside, and he becomes טמא and counts as 'entered' at the very same instant. No body part goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: a dying person, still alive
his soul left, meaning he died
while he was sitting

steps.whatToRemember: Normal walking into a house cannot give two liabilities, because some part of the body always goes in first. The two real cases are: (1) רב פפא: being uncovered inside a protective container, and (2) מר בר רב אשי: someone dies while you are already inside.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
For example, where he entered when the person there was dying,
and that person's soul left while he was sitting there.
So impurity and entering come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּעָיֵיל כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹסֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different case alongside רב פפא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an alternative case where the impurity begins after he is fully inside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impurity must already be in the house when he enters.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the death happens while he is inside, טומאה and ביאה begin together.

steps.title: A ברייתא: טומאת מת begins only at death
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from two different פסוקים that a person does not give off טומאת מת until he actually dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: from the word "to profane himself" we learn that the impurity does not start until the person dies. רבי says: from "when they die he becomes impure" we learn it does not start until he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two sources teaching the same rule: טומאת מת begins only at the moment of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion learns it from the פסוק about a כהן, "להחלו". רבי learns it from the פסוק about a נזיר, "במותם". This fits the earlier cases, where a person becomes טמא at the exact moment the other person dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (this opens a ברייתא)
"To profane himself", said about a כֹּהֵן becoming טמא
"When they die", said about a נָזִיר and his relatives
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"To profane himself": not until the moment that he dies.
רבי says:
"When they die" he becomes impure: not until he dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on when טומאת מת begins. This is the same point the earlier cases depended on, where someone becomes טמא at the moment of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person does not give off טומאת מת until he has actually died. One opinion learns this from להחלו and רבי learns it from במותם.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why there are two opinions if both seem to teach the same rule. This question sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions end with "until he dies", so they seem to agree. The גמרא wants to know whether anything changes depending on which פסוק we use.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a practical difference between learning the rule from להחלו and learning it from במותם?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Only the source verse is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there is no practical difference. The two opinions only disagree about which פסוק teaches the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is only which verse they interpret.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that both opinions have the same הלכה. They only argue about where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, nothing changes in practice. The argument is only about which פסוק is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Which verse they explain: a difference in the source only, not in practice
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
The verse they interpret is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means there is no difference in הלכה at all. They just learn it from different פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no practical difference. The only difference is which פסוק is the source.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: They differ about a dying person
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the opinions differ about a גוסס. Using להחלו, even a גוסס is included. Using במותם, only someone who has actually died is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the difference between them is a dying person. According to the one who learns from "to profane himself", even a dying person is included. According to the one who learns from "when they die", once he has died, yes; a dying person, no.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different answer. He says there is a real practical difference: the case of a גוסס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the one who learns from להחלו, a גוסס is already included. For the one who learns from במותם, the word "die" means only an actual death counts, so a גוסס is not included. This turns the argument into a disagreement in הלכה, not just about the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A person in his final dying moments who is still alive
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third opinion in the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are two אמוראים explaining the difference between the two opinions in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
A dying person is the difference between them.
According to the one who says it is from "to profane himself":
even a dying person is included.
According to the one who says it is from "when they die":
once he has died, yes; a dying person, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: גּוֹסֵס אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 9 that disagrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two opinions differ about a גוסס: להחלו includes him, and במותם does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya (Steps 12-21) follows ריש לקיש's approach. It checks whether each side has a use for the other side's פסוק, and then tests the להחלו side against a משנה.

steps.title: What does the להחלו side do with במותם?
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, the גמרא asks the להחלו side: the Torah also wrote במותם, so what does that word teach you?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says it is from "to profane himself": but it is written "when they die"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the להחלו opinion. The word במותם seems to say impurity starts only at death, so how can he include a גוסס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If במותם means "only once they have actually died", it seems to argue against including a גוסס. The להחלו side has to explain what that word is there for.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (used to bring a פסוק as a challenge)

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is from "to profane himself":
but it is written "when they die"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the להחלו side of ריש לקיש's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The להחלו opinion, which includes a גוסס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's word במותם seems to limit impurity to actual death, which goes against including a גוסס.

steps.title: במותם teaches that a נזיר may become טמא from other impurities
steps.stepSummary: The להחלו side uses במותם for רבי's other teaching. Only from his relatives' death is a נזיר forbidden to become טמא. He may become טמא from their צרעת or their זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי, as it was taught: רבי says, "when they die" he may not become impure, but he may become impure from their leprosy and from their discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word במותם is not about timing at all for this opinion. It teaches which kind of טומאה a נזיר must stay away from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: במותם teaches that only טומאת מת is forbidden to a נזיר. Other kinds of טומאה from his relatives, like צרעת or זיבה, are allowed. So the word has a different job and does not exclude a גוסס.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Their צָרַעַת (the skin disease)
Their זִיבָה, a discharge that makes a person טמא
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of רבי.
As it was taught: רבי says:
In their death he may not become impure,
but he may become impure from their leprosy and from their discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: במותם seemed to teach that impurity begins only at actual death, which would exclude a גוסס.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the להחלו side, במותם teaches that a נזיר is forbidden only to become טמא מת, not to become טמא from צרעת or זיבה.

steps.title: But the במותם side also needs the word for רבי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the במותם side: you need במותם for the teaching about צרעת and זיבה, so how can you also learn the timing rule from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says it is from "when they die": but he needs it for this reasoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the other side. One word seems to be doing two jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that במותם teaches that only death-impurity is forbidden to a נזיר. If so, the במותם side seems to have no extra word left to teach that a גוסס is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: But he needs it (for something else)!
Reasoning, here meaning the teaching just mentioned

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is from "when they die":
but he needs it for this reasoning!
phrases.notes: "This reasoning" is רבי's teaching from Step 13 about צרעת and זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּמוֹתָם הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהַאי סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer from Step 13 against the במותם side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The במותם opinion, which excludes a גוסס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: במותם is already used for the teaching about צרעת and זיבה, so it cannot also be the source for the timing rule.

steps.title: The extra letters in במותם teach both rules
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written במות but wrote במותם. The longer word lets us learn two rules from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say "when [he] dies". Why does it say "when they die"? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word במותם is longer than it needs to be. That extra wording is enough to teach both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah wanted to teach only one thing, the shorter במות would have been enough. The fuller form במותם shows there is room to learn two rules. Impurity starts only at actual death (so not from a גוסס), and a נזיר is forbidden only to become טמא מת.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say (the shorter way)
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the two sources differ only in which פסוק is used. ריש לקיש says they differ about a גוסס. So far, each side can explain במותם. For the להחלו side, במותם teaches only רבי's rule about צרעת and זיבה. For the במותם side, the longer word במותם teaches two things: impurity starts only at actual death, and a נזיר is forbidden only to become טמא מת. The next steps (16-19) check the word להחלו the same way.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "when [he] dies".
Why does it say "when they die"?
Learn from it two things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows two teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word can teach only one rule, so the במותם side would have no source to exclude a גוסס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because במותם is fuller than במות, it teaches both that impurity starts only at actual death and that a נזיר is forbidden only to become טמא מת.

steps.title: What does the במותם side learn from להחלו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the other side: if you learn the rule from ״במותם״, what do you do with the word ״להחלו״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says the source is ״במותם״, isn't ״להחלו״ also written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. It now challenges the ״במותם״ side to explain the word ״להחלו״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the ״להחלו״ side had to explain ״במותם״. Now the ״במותם״ side must show that ״להחלו״ is not an extra word for him. Every word in the תורה needs a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it written? Used to point to a word in the פסוק that seems to need a use
"To profane himself". A word from the פסוק about a כהן becoming טמא

phrases.english: And according to the one who says "when they die",
isn't "to profane himself" written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 12. After defending the ״להחלו״ side, the גמרא now challenges the ״במותם״ side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ״במותם״ side of ריש לקיש's explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״במותם״ is the source, the word ״להחלו״ seems to have no job.

steps.title: להחלו excludes someone already profaned
steps.stepSummary: ״להחלו״ teaches that the ban on becoming טמא applies only to someone who is not yet טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״להחלו״ comes to teach this: the ban applies to one who is not yet profaned. That excludes one who is already profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the ״במותם״ side a different use for ״להחלו״. Someone who is already טמא is not forbidden to become טמא again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״להחלו״ means "to make himself profane". That only makes sense for a person who is still holy and pure. If he is already טמא, there is nothing left to profane, so the ban does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes for this purpose
Profaned, here meaning already טמא
Already standing in a profaned state

phrases.english: "To profane himself" comes for this:
for one who is not profaned,
excluding this one, who is already profaned.
phrases.notes: Someone who is already טמא is not forbidden to become טמא again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by giving ״להחלו״ its own teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: ״להחלו״ teaches that someone already טמא is not forbidden to become טמא again.

steps.title: Can the להחלו side use one word for two rules?
steps.stepSummary: The ״להחלו״ side needs the word for the rule about someone already טמא. So how can it also teach the rule about a גוסס?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns from ״להחלו״, he needs that word for this other idea!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ״להחלו״ side. Everyone needs ״להחלו״ for the rule just taught in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 14. Normally one word teaches one rule. If ״להחלו״ is already busy excluding someone who is already טמא, it seems unable to teach that a גוסס counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else
Here, a teaching or idea

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is learned from "to profane himself",
he needs it for this idea!
phrases.notes: "This idea" is the rule from step 17: one who is already טמא is not included.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִ״לְּהֵחַלּוֹ״, הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהַאי סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 17 to challenge the ״להחלו״ side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ״להחלו״ side, which learns the גוסס rule from ״להחלו״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word normally teaches one rule. ״להחלו״ is already used for the rule about someone already טמא.

steps.title: The longer word teaches two rules
steps.stepSummary: The תורה could have written ״להחל״. Writing ״להחלו״ allows two rules to be learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said ״להחל״. Why does it say ״להחלו״? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra letter in ״להחלו״ gives room for a second teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is built just like step 15. ״להחל״ alone would teach one rule. The added ending ״ו״ in ״להחלו״ shows the word carries two rules: the rule about a גוסס and the rule about someone already טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, let the פסוק say...
You learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides are now complete. ״להחלו״ and ״במותם״ are each longer than needed. So each side can learn two rules from its word.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "to profane";
what is "to profane himself"?
You learn from it two things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 the same way step 15 answered step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording allows a double teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: The longer form ״להחלו״ teaches both the גוסס rule and the rule about someone already טמא.

steps.title: A משנה says a גוסס does not make others טמא
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a person only makes others טמא once his soul leaves, even if he is a גוסס. This seems to go against the ״להחלו״ side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a person does not make others טמא until his soul leaves. This is true even if he is badly wounded, and even if he is a גוסס. But the ״להחלו״ side says a גוסס counts, and this teaching says he does not make others טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to argue with the ״להחלו״ side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ״להחלו״ side said a כהן or נזיר is already affected by a גוסס. But the משנה says clearly that a גוסס does not make others טמא at all. So how can a גוסס count?

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, by bringing an earlier teaching
Until his soul leaves
Badly cut or wounded
A person in the last stage before death

phrases.english: They challenged: A person does not make others impure
until his soul leaves,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: even if badly wounded and even if dying.
But according to the one who says it is learned from "to profane himself",
it teaches that he does not make others impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides are defended from the פסוקים, the גמרא challenges the ״להחלו״ side from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ״להחלו״ side, which says even a גוסס counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a גוסס does not make others טמא. So how can a גוסס affect a כהן?

steps.title: Making others טמא versus becoming profaned
steps.stepSummary: A גוסס does not make others טמא until he dies. But a כהן is already considered profaned by him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For making others טמא, he must wait until his soul leaves. For becoming profaned, the כהן is already profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the question into two separate laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is only about when a person makes others טמא. That happens only after death. The ״להחלו״ side is about a different law: whether a כהן is profaned by being near him. That can happen already while the person is a גוסס.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding making others טמא
Regarding becoming profaned
He is profaned

steps.whatToRemember: A גוסס does not make anyone טמא. But according to the ״להחלו״ side, a כהן is already profaned by being with him. These are two separate laws.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a גוסס is treated as dead. He makes no one טמא. The only new point is that a כהן is already profaned by him.

phrases.english: Regarding making impure, it waits until his soul leaves;
regarding being profaned, he is already profaned.
phrases.notes: The one who is profaned is the כהן who is with the גוסס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by showing the משנה deals with a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say a גוסס has no effect at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about making others טמא. Being profaned already starts with a גוסס.
